passages.provision_quote: Except in a medical emergency, a physician may not intentionally or knowingly perform, induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion if the probable gestational age of the unborn human being has been determined to be greater than fifteen weeks.
passages.note: A 15-week cutoff with a medical-emergency-only exception does not match rung 3's first-trimester clause or rung 2's through-second-trimester clause.
Overview page confirms House Third Reading passage of this single-subject gestational-limit bill, later signed by the governor.
Roll call shows Pingerelli voting Yes on House Third Reading of the 15-week gestational-limit bill.

rows.reasoning: Pingerelli voted Yes on SB1164's House Third Reading, a single-subject bill barring abortion after fifteen weeks' gestation except in a medical emergency. Fifteen weeks is past the first trimester named in rung 3 and far short of the second-trimester endpoint named in rung 2, and the 'medical emergency' exception is narrower than either rung's 'protect the mother's health' exception, so the vote shows a restrictive direction without matching either rung's clauses.
needs_source: a statement from Pingerelli explaining her vote or describing her own position on the 15-week limit, to settle whether it matches rung 2 or rung 3
